title: Counting expressions: singular noun
summary: Use the singular partitive noun after basic numbers greater than one and after monta.
objectives: Use the singular partitive noun after basic numbers greater than one and after monta.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use the singular partitive noun after basic numbers greater than one and after monta.
A phrase can name several things while its noun stays singular in form. Compare one book with two books: the counting pattern, not English plural spelling, controls the Finnish noun.
This lesson uses uninflected counting expressions. It does not teach number words in other cases. Monta also takes a singular partitive noun.
keyPoints: After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural.

steps: After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural.
Kaksi means “two” and works as the quantity word. kaksi is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
kirjaa means “book” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.
After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural.
Kolme means “three” and works as the quantity word. kolme is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
autoa means “car” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Add -a to auto: autoa. The ending is selected from the word’s back vowels.
After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural.
Neljä means “four” and works as the quantity word. neljä is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
kuppia means “cup” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep strong pp and the final i: kuppi + a = kuppia.
After these basic counting expressions, use the singular partitive noun. Two or more referents do not make the noun’s grammatical form plural.
Monta means “many” and works as the quantity word. monta is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
lelua means “toy” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep lelu and add -a because u is a back vowel: lelua.

commonMistakes: Do not attach the nominative plural -t after a basic counting number.
Do not use a plural partitive after kaksi, kolme or neljä in these phrases.
